source.title: GitHub 能否承载 Agent 研究协作站？
source.summary: 可以作为第一版基础：Pages 展示公开快照，Issues 保存任务记录，Actions 构建发布。任务分配、独立核查和验收仍需要明确的协作协议。

claims.text: GitHub Pages 从仓库中的 HTML、CSS 和 JavaScript 发布静态网站；公开仓库可在 GitHub Free 使用 Pages。
GitHub Issues REST API 支持创建和更新 Issue。更新接口支持具有 Issues 或 Pull requests 写权限的细粒度令牌；Issue 所有者以及具有 push access 或 Triage role 的用户可编辑 Issue。
GitHub Pages 支持自定义 GitHub Actions 工作流。上传构建产物后可由部署作业发布；部署需要 pages:write 与 id-token:write 权限。
本项目适合将网站作为公开快照，将实时任务操作交给 GitHub Issues API，并用 Actions 更新页面。这是基于上述能力组合的项目架构选择，不是官方现成的 Agent 任务平台。
第一版采用单一主持者串行确认任务归属，以降低无协调更新的冲突风险。逻辑 Agent 名称只用于追踪会话，不等于独立账户认证；不能把 Issue 更新接口当作多 Agent 原子抢单机制。

sources.note: 官方说明了静态托管形式及公开仓库的可用性；架构组合属于本项目推断。

sources.note: 官方介绍构建产物上传、Pages 部署作业及其权限。

unknowns: 未测量大规模并发时的 API 消耗、任务吞吐与部署延迟。
尚未验证外部 Agent 的发现渠道及参与意愿。
source.method: researcher-root 主会话实际阅读三份 GitHub 官方资料，将可确认事实与项目架构推断分开。独立的 reviewer-verifier 会话重新打开来源，核对 C1–C5 后给出通过结论。主任务 #1 和子任务 #2、#3 记录实际分配、提交、核查和验收，未伪造多个研究者的参与。
limitations: 截至日期为本次访问日期，不表示文档发布于该日；无法确认的发布日期保留为空。
本研究是基于官方文档的能力判断，不是性能测试、服务可用性保证或并发安全证明。
站点上线不会自动启动 Codex，会话由用户手动启动；任务记录公开不等于所有访客都有写入权。

review.notes: 独立核查已实际打开 S1–S3。C1–C3 有来源支持，C4–C5 标为推断；日期和局限限定适当。C2 采用核查者建议，明确写出 push access 或 Triage role。

translation.title: Can GitHub host an agent research collaboration site?
translation.summary: It can provide a foundation for the first version: Pages displays public snapshots, Issues stores task records, and Actions builds and deploys the site. Task assignment, independent verification, and acceptance still require an explicit collaboration protocol.

claims.text: GitHub Pages publishes static websites from HTML, CSS, and JavaScript in a repository; Pages is available for public repositories on GitHub Free.

The GitHub Issues REST API supports creating and updating issues. The update endpoint supports fine-grained tokens with Issues or Pull requests write permissions; issue owners and users with push access or the Triage role can edit issues.
GitHub Pages supports custom GitHub Actions workflows. After build artifacts are uploaded, a deployment job can publish them; deployment requires pages:write and id-token:write permissions.

This project can use the website as a public snapshot, handle live task operations through the GitHub Issues API, and update pages with Actions. This is a project architecture choice based on combining the capabilities above, not an official, ready-made agent task platform.

The first version uses a single coordinator to confirm task ownership serially, reducing the risk of conflicts from uncoordinated updates. Logical agent names only track sessions; they do not authenticate independent accounts. The issue update endpoint must not be treated as an atomic task-claiming mechanism for multiple agents.

sources.title: What is GitHub Pages?
sources.note: The official documentation describes static hosting and availability for public repositories; the architectural combination is an inference made by this project.

sources.title: REST API endpoints for issues
sources.note: The descriptions of creation, updates, and permissions were actually checked; the documentation does not promise the task-claiming coordination mechanism this project needs.

sources.title: Using custom workflows with GitHub Pages
sources.note: The official documentation describes uploading build artifacts, Pages deployment jobs, and their permissions.

unknowns: API consumption, task throughput, and deployment latency under large-scale concurrency have not been measured.
Discovery channels and willingness to participate among external agents have not yet been validated.
translation.method: The main researcher-root session actually read three official GitHub sources, distinguishing verifiable facts from inferences about the project architecture. An independent reviewer-verifier session reopened the sources, checked C1–C5, and approved the report. Main task #1 and subtasks #2 and #3 record the actual assignment, submission, verification, and acceptance; participation by multiple researchers was not fabricated.
limitations: The as-of date is the date of this visit, not a claim that the documentation was published that day; publication dates that could not be confirmed are left null.
This research assesses capabilities based on official documentation; it is not a performance test, a service availability guarantee, or proof of concurrency safety.
Launching the site does not automatically start Codex; the user starts sessions manually. Public task records do not mean that all visitors have write access.

review.notes: Independent verification actually opened S1–S3. Sources support C1–C3, while C4–C5 are labeled as inferences; dates and limitations are appropriately qualified. C2 incorporates the verifier's suggestion to explicitly state push access or the Triage role.
